title: U.S. Stocks Fall on Hot Inflation Report, AI Sell-Off
source_used: Yahoo Finance / The Motley Fool / Benzinga
key_facts: US stocks fell on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 as September inflation came in hotter than expected.
Consumer prices rose 3.7% year on year in September, up from 3.4% in August (Bureau of Labor Statistics, per Benzinga).
Nasdaq Composite fell 1.88% to 26,692.87; S&P 500 fell 1.11% to 7,718.94.
Chip stocks led the fall; Nvidia closed down more than 3% (Yahoo Finance).
Stubborn inflation revived fears that the Federal Reserve will raise rates again (Motley Fool).
The PHLX Semiconductor index had fallen over 10% in five days (Motley Fool).
CoreWeave fell more than 16% after a chart of its bond yields circulated online.
quote_evidence: Major indexes fell this morning as stubborn inflation revived fears that the Federal Reserve will hike rates again, pressuring growth stocks.
The Consumer Price Index rose 3.7% in September, higher than economists had expected.

The sell-off in chip stocks deepened on Wednesday as a hotter-than-expected inflation read raised worries about more rate hikes by the Federal Reserve and a higher cost of capital, potentially throwing a wrench into the AI trade.
why_it_matters_hint: Higher borrowing costs hit the AI trade because AI build-outs rely on debt.
notes: WSJ headline only was available; see notes.
